title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were pulled over in Colwich, Kansas, after a Flock camera flagged their minivan as possibly stolen. Their KU Alumni plate had the number 7007. Police found a stolen GMC pickup had a temporary Kansas tag with the same number but a different background. The wrong plate type had been entered into the system. The couple was stopped again about a month later in Catoosa, Oklahoma, where officers drew guns and handcuffed Matthew before realizing the mistake.

Wichita police Capt. Casey Slaughter said Flock cameras read only numbers and letters, not plate designs. Kansas has more than 100 plate designs, about half specialty plates, and duplicates numbers. The state is moving from six digit to seven digit, non duplicated plate numbers. Wichita police have discussed training Flock's AI to recognize plate backgrounds. The Spurlocks' stolen vehicle entry has expired, so they no longer expect stops, and they hope to keep their 14 year old KU plate.
